title: Going to work for the L&N Railroad
summary: From October 1936 Joe worked for the railroad and drifted away from music; he describes his jobs from Red Cap to the freight depot.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: And uh... Well, let's say I played with uh... Paul Maurice for quite a number of years. I don't know, I went to work for the railroad. And that was in the lower part of 36. 1936, October of the exact. And uh... Somehow or another, I had practically got away from music. So uh... I worked there for the L&N Railroad, which I'm chilling for it by now. Uh-huh. I work in Yorlma every day, except for Saturday and Sunday.
Yeah, I commute back to the college. I've been working with my son.
What do you do for him? Beg your pardon? What do you do for the L&N?

Well uh... When I first started, I started as a Red Cap. Then I went on as a baggage and mail puller. And train puller. And dining car. I've done just the fact that everything can be done for the railroad. What do you do now? Well now I'm at the Freight Depot. Allen Freight. Uh... That's uh... I went out there after the changeover to Union time. I didn't go to the time. I was there. I was just there with the L&N. So that's where I'm located now. Well, let's say back... What is it? 62, uh... Let's say around... Late 40s. I'll go back maybe... I should probably 48. Uh... The same boy, Harry, matching to you. Uh... Edgar Benwell. We call him Buddy Bo.
